title: Steerpoint: Reflect & Reset — Company Huddle
summary: Leadership framed progress against Q2 reliability and cost targets, announced a limited hiring runway, introduced a culture thermostat initiative, and committed to three operational experiments (autoscaling cadence, prefix caching pilot, and a streamlined on-call rotation). Q&A covered return-to-office guidance and compensation transparency. Action items and follow-ups were assigned.

transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate the time. We're gonna run about an hour, short updates from execs and then open Q&A.
[00:14] Ravi Kapoor: Quick context — last month we had two Sev2 incidents, both related to prefix cache invalidation under burst. We fixed the immediate rollouts but we need durable mitigations.
[00:29] Speaker 3 (maybe Leah): Yeah and to add, from product standpoint some customers saw latency spikes on longer contexts, so we've prioritized a small kernel change and an infra config tweak.
[00:47] Samir Patel: The mitigation path is threefold: patch the cache eviction logic, add a short-lived prefix cache for high QPS routes, and tune our autoscaler thresholds. We'll run a staged rollout to Dedicated first.
[01:05] Leah Ortega: On roadmap, this delays a minor Optimize UI change but shouldn't affect major launches. We will also re-evaluate telemetry to catch these patterns earlier.
[01:22] Maya Lin: Switching to people updates — headcount runway is slimmer than we hoped. We are not in a hiring freeze exactly, but hiring will be targeted to critical roles only for the next 8 weeks.
[01:36] Ava Martinez: I want to emphasize we are protecting the core product and SRE hiring to keep reliability up. We also plan to defer some non-essential contractor renewals.
[01:52] Jordan Reed: Some engineers flagged that the on-call load is uneven; infra is trying a 4-week rotation but it's burnout-y. I'll propose a 2-week light/on-call + 2-week backup model.
[02:10] Ravi Kapoor: That ties to cost as well — longer rotations reduce context switches, shorter rotations reduce fatigue; trade-off.
[02:22] [02:22] (crowd murmur)
[02:25] Speaker 4: Quick question: will RTO expectations change with this targeted hiring?
[02:29] Ava Martinez: Short answer: no immediate company-wide change. Teams can set local hybrid agreements within the guidelines. We will publish clarified guidance tomorrow.
[02:39] Maya Lin: We'll also start the "culture thermostat" initiative — two-minute pulse checks monthly and quarterly anonymous micro-surveys focused on psychological safety and workload.
[02:55] Speaker 1: Who will see the survey results?
[02:58] Maya Lin: Execs and managers will see aggregated results; anonymized slices will be shared company-wide, no raw responses distributed.
[03:09] Leah Ortega: Back to product, we're accelerating a prefix caching pilot on Hosted API for a subset of customers to measure token-cost improvements and tail latency. This is low-risk and reversible.
[03:24] Samir Patel: We'll put telemetry dashboards for that pilot (per-customer latency, cache hit-rate, per-token CPU) and share weekly.
[03:34] Ravi Kapoor: On the research side, we have a PR for a kernel path that improves kv-cache hits for long sequences, credit to the runtime team. If tests pass, we'll canary it next week.
[03:48] [03:48] Speaker 2 (interrupting): Sorry, is there any immediate customer exposure?
[03:50] Leah Ortega: We notified top-tier customers and offered an opt-out; no escalations so far.
[03:58] Ava Martinez: I want to acknowledge the team — shipping that patch under pressure was solid work.
[04:07] [04:07] (applause, brief)
[04:12] Jordan Reed: On compensation transparency — people asked about promotion cadence and comp bands. We've got a plan: HR will publish band ranges and promotion criteria by next month, and individual managers will run calibration meetings.
[04:25] Maya Lin: We'll also schedule an AMA specifically on compensation and career ladders.
[04:30] Speaker 5: Any guidance for folks on interview pipeline?
[04:33] Leah Ortega: Interviews continue; we just prioritize by impact. If you're owning product lines with high reliability burden, we'll prioritize those hires.
[04:41] [04:41] (crosstalk)
[04:45] Ava Martinez: Experimentation slate — three operational experiments: 1) Autoscaling cadence change (shorter cooldowns for spike workloads), 2) Prefix cache pilot for Hosted routes, 3) Rotated on-call trial to reduce burnout. Teams can opt in.
[05:05] Samir Patel: We'll publish experiment metrics and success criteria. For instance, autoscaling change: target 20% lower p95 for cold-start events without >10% cost increase.
[05:18] Speaker 6: How will we measure morale for the culture thermostat?
[05:20] Maya Lin: We'll track NPS-like question (would you recommend working here), anonymous free-text tagged for themes, and manager follow-ups where there are negative signal clusters.
[05:34] Ava Martinez: Financials — spending is up on GPU hours vs plan due to some heavy benchmarking in April. We're pulling back non-critical large-scale experiments and leaning on Dedicated reserved capacity for long-running tests to save unit cost.
[05:53] Ravi Kapoor: We will also tighten access to large dev clusters and require a short business-case for >24h runs.
[06:01] [06:01] Speaker 7: Any update on Private / on-prem sales traction?
[06:04] Leah Ortega: Private is doing fine; a few enterprise deals in procurement, but sales cycles remain long. We're doubling down on compliance docs to speed procurement.
[06:15] Ava Martinez: Quick shout-out to Solutions for the work on the compliance pack. That helped one POC move to legal review.
[06:25] Jordan Reed: Technical note: we're rolling a small change to the serving runtime that reduces memory overhead for nvme-backed kv stores — hope to cut some per-token memory previously allocated.
[06:38] Samir Patel: That memory reduction plus batch tuning should show up as smaller host counts for some workloads. We'll put numbers in the cost audit.
[06:47] [06:47] (brief silence, typing)
[06:52] Ava Martinez: Ok Q&A — start feeding Qs into Slido, but we also have a mic open.
[06:58] Speaker 8: Are there any reorgs planned? Rumors on Slack say platform will move under infra.
[07:05] Ava Martinez: No planned reorgs today. We are exploring small reporting tweaks to reduce service handoffs but not full org changes. We'll be explicit before anything lands.
[07:16] Speaker 9: Request for better incident postmortems visibility — some say they're hard to find.
[07:21] Ravi Kapoor: Good point — we'll centralize postmortems in a single read-only repo and tag related tickets; infra will own that by next week.
[07:33] Maya Lin: Final note — mental health resources and a manager-support program will run next month.
[07:38] Ava Martinez: Great — thank you. Recap: publish guidance tomorrow, run culture survey, Samir cost audit, Leah hiring list, teams pick experiments. We'll do a shorter follow-up all-hands in two weeks focused on exec Q&A.
[07:56] [07:56] (meeting ends)
